title: Pre Shot Routine Same Every Time (Chas McIvor)
style: Country rock with bluegrass influences. Features a prominent banjo playing rapid rolls, a clean electric guitar with light overdrive, and a driving drum kit with a heavy backbeat. A deep baritone male vocal delivers spoken-word and sung passages. The bass guitar follows a walking pattern. The arrangement includes a fiddle playing melodic fills and a breakdown section with a prominent banjo solo. Tempo is 145 BPM in the key of G major.
lyrics:
[Intro]
[banjo rolls, electric guitar stabs, drum fill]
[spoken]
I say son, every shot starts behind the ball. See it, feel it, trust it, swing it. Same routine, every single time.

[Verse 1]
[driving drums, walking bass]
Stand behind the ball, six feet back
Pick the target, pick the line, pick the track
Visualize the ball flight, see it land
Feel the swing in your body, not just your hands
Three practice swings, feel the tempo then step in
Align the clubface first, body parallel left of the target line
One look, two look, swing in the time

[Chorus]
[full band, fiddle enters]
Preshot routine, same every time, son
Behind the ball then the work begun
See it, feel it, align it, swing it
Twelve seconds total, never split it

[Verse 2]
[banjo rolls continue]
Clubface aimed at the target first
Feet, hips, shoulders parallel left, the rehearsed verse
One waggle, two waggle, look at the target, back to the ball
Swing within the carpet

[Bridge]
[drums drop to half-time, bass sustains]
[spoken]
I say boy, the routine is the anchor. When the pressure rises, the routine is the answer. Same twelve seconds, calm and slow. Trust the work, son. Let it go.

[Chorus]
[full band, high energy]
Preshot routine, same every time, son
Behind the ball then the work begun
See it, feel it, align it, swing it
Twelve seconds total, never split it

[Outro]
[fiddle solo, banjo rolls]
See it, feel it, trust it, swing it
Same twelve seconds, don't fight it
Routine is the rock when the pressure's on
Whoa-oh, that's my boy
That's the treasure
[final banjo flourish, drum hit]
